summary:
Our challenge was to develop a health-monitoring program for astronauts. We decided to make a web app that helps astronauts monitor their own health quickly and efficiently, all in one place. The app is easy to access on any internet-connected device. They can use the app to log their personal health information, including blood and urine test results, by logging into their account. This helps to assess the risk of any health issues that the astronaut may encounter. There are guides and tips in the Learn section to give guidance to the astronaut in case there are problems. A mental health check is included. The astronaut can talk to their flight surgeon for extra support if needed in the Messages tab. 
A flight surgeon has a different layout, where they respond to people in space and help answer their questions. The astronauts' status is sent to the flight surgeon to provide additional context to enhance the flight surgeon's response. The flight surgeon is a human who gives qualified answers and instructions to the astronaut using their own login. 
Health data is entered using a dedicated tab. There is a streak for each astronaut to enter their health data every day. Trackers for sleep, heart rate, glucose, blood pressure, water intake, breaths per minute, and blood oxygen are included as bar graphs. The bars are color-coded to show whether the levels are normal, concerning, or critical.
details:
What does it do or how does it work?

We aim to maintain the astronaut in ongoing space missions healthy and create a safe and stable working environment for all astronauts. Our app 11:56 assist astronauts in monitoring their health during spaceflight through taking input from various ways and provide solutions through consulting a flight surgeons on the app to cure the astronauts in poor health condition. We achieve this through:

Each astronaut could create their own instance on the app using a username and password, and could log on onto the app using it.

They wear a wristband which is similar to a smartwatch on Earth which could record the health data that we have to monitor. The astronauts will then manually input the data into the app. Tracked data includes water intake, blood oxygen, blood pressure, breathing rate, and many more.

Using the health data, the app uses alerts to remind astronauts of abnormal health data, and suggests ways to improve their health accordingly. An exercise plan is also suggested to astronauts depending on their situation

We have tests for data that cannot be measured by equipment such as reaction time and a mental health evaluation test which would contribute to their mental health score.

An astronaut could consult flight surgeons through the built-in messaging system on the app. The flight surgeons could then provide solutions to their problems as they are able to view the health data and flagged for each astronaut. The messages sent to the astronaut have high importance so they couldn't miss it, and this makes sure that astronauts are constantly taking care of their health.

What benefits does it have?

Our project helps astronauts monitor their health quickly and efficiently, all in one app, using simple tests and daily health logs with a streak as long as there is an internet-connected device. There are trackers for sleep, heart rate, glucose, blood pressure, water intake, breaths per minute, and blood oxygen as bar graphs. The bars are color-coded to show whether the levels are normal, concerning, or critical to alert the user. The flight surgeon can be directly messaged by the astronaut user to give instructions and advice, with the astronaut's condition included with the message as context for the surgeon's response.

What is the intended impact of the project?

Our intended impact is to provide astronauts with improved health software, this means that astronauts can ensure that they are at peak physical condition when performing extensive tasks such as space walks and maintenance. By providing an easy and accessible UI, astronauts will feel more motivated to record vitals due to the action being less draining. This allows data to be produced more extensively allowing experts to efficiently create new technologies.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?

We used Python (Flask) for the backend and used CSS and HTML for the frontend. We also used Figma for creating parts of the user interface and used AI to convert the Figma design into HTML and CSS code. JavaScript is used for front-end scripts as well. Markdown is used for writing the learning content for the astronauts which is then converted to HTML and CSS automatically by our handler script.

Our main IDE used by the team was PyCharm by JetBrains.

We used Claude, Github Copilot and Junie to accelerate our development. All ideas and logic were made by the team.

How is your project creative?

Our project is a simple and innovative solution for astronauts to access their vitals, something that is commonly overlooked as astronauts are unable to access advanced health information regularly, being far out of Earth. Instead of monitoring copious amounts of data, we look at vitals that may be menial on its own, but over time we can see how the astronaut's condition fluctuates.

What factors did your team consider?

Our team considered making the app simple to allow astronauts to save time, we did this to ensure that the app is user friendly while providing accurate and concise data.
